items.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022
items.q: But one day before, Woody comes up to me and says, “You know, Frank, we need a hot number.” I says, “Have I got a hot number for you.” And so we performed it.

ctx.x: That’s the greatest part of that actually, the reason why I stayed there for all of those years is because everybody came in — you take Tony Klatka, Alan Broadbent, Bill Stapleton, they all come in — they wrote what they wanted to and he would just approve it every time. And I mean Alan Vizutti, you know, the trumpet player, he’d come in with the “Fire Dance” and my tunes too. But he wasn’t there when my tunes — actually I think so, no, I don’t think he ever heard my tunes. But no, I mean you know Fedchock did a…

was planned. All the sessions were planned. But one day before, Woody comes up to me and says, “You know, Frank, we need a hot number.” I says, “Have I got a hot number for you.” And so we performed it. I wonder if you ever heard of the tune, I don’t know if you have.
Yes I have. It was like how much time did you get to rehearse it?

items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: So he came out with us, he was already a mature man.

ctx.x: Yeah, no wonder he's so enterprising.
So he's had a big history and a big background with that. But he also decided that this is the way you find life. So he came out with us, he was already a mature man.
Well, it's interesting that -- he plays that unofficial role for the band.
